RE-CON-026.explanation: Dual agency is lawful only with the informed written consent of both principals, and some states prohibit it entirely. In Massachusetts, M.G.L. c. 112, section 87AAA 3/4(b) and 254 CMR 3.00(13)(b) require informed written consent of buyer and seller on the Board's form. Telling only the seller leaves the buyer unaware of the divided loyalty.

RE-CON-027.explanation: In designated agency the broker assigns separate licensees to each client within the same firm; Massachusetts allows it with written consent under 254 CMR 3.00(13)(c), and the appointing broker is then presumed a dual agent. RE-CON-040.explanation: Agency disclosure should come before a consumer shares confidential information. In Massachusetts the Board's form is given at the first personal meeting to discuss a specific property, and at an open house a sign or listing literature may conspicuously disclose the agency instead (254 CMR 3.00(13)(a)). Collecting his maximum price first would let him reveal information that the seller's agent must share with her client.

RE-PRAC-002.explanation: Earnest money belongs in the broker's escrow account, so the salesperson delivers it to the broker. In Massachusetts, 254 CMR 3.00(10)(c) says a salesperson must immediately turn over all deposit money to the employing broker and may never hold client funds. Handing it to the seller or holding it personally breaches the duty to account for client funds.

The rules require disclosure, not testing or removal.
